findings.description: The gender dimension in the research methodology is addressed solely as an institutional GEP compliance obligation, not as a research-methodology consideration. The MSCA-PF evaluation form requires 'consideration of the gender dimension...if relevant for the research project' as a component of the soundness of methodology sub-criterion (weight 50%). The observable proposal content — the implementation section and assembled draft consistency log — frames gender exclusively as a host-institution legal requirement. Precision agriculture research involving irrigation decision-support has documented gender-differentiated dimensions (smallholder farmworker demographics, differential technology adoption, access to irrigation decision authority) that are neither acknowledged as relevant nor dismissed with a principled argument. No evidence of research-methodology-level gender dimension analysis appears in any readable section artifact.
findings.evidence: Implementation section 3.1 ethics self-assessment: 'Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, as a higher education establishment in an EU Member State, is required to have a gender equality plan in place at grant signature and throughout the fellowship.' This is an institutional compliance statement, not a research-methodology gender dimension analysis.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated paragraph in the Excellence section's methodology sub-section explicitly assessing whether and how gender dimension is relevant to the research project. If relevant (e.g., gendered agricultural labour patterns, differential farmer technology adoption in Hungarian horticulture), articulate how it is considered in study design, validation cohort selection, or stakeholder engagement. If assessed as not relevant to this specific research context, provide a principled one-paragraph justification. Do not substitute the GEP institutional compliance statement for this analysis.

findings.description: Inter-sectoral training exposure within WP4 is limited. AgroVIR's role is explicitly scoped to field access, validation logistics, and farmer feedback at Hungarian tomato sites — it has no formal training or mentoring contribution to the fellow. No non-academic sector secondment or structured placement is included. The supervisor's entrepreneurial track record (co-founder of Cubert GmbH and Brightic Research) is mentioned in the implementation section's hosting narrative but is not structured into any formal inter-sectoral training activity within WP4. MSCA-PF evaluators assess the quality of supervision and training — including inter-sectoral exposure — under the Excellence criterion's supervision and two-way transfer sub-criterion.
findings.evidence: Implementation section 3.2: 'AgroVIR does not own or operate the decision-support tool; its contribution is to make real tomato farms accessible for the WP3 validation campaigns...to facilitate farmer feedback on the research demonstrator (MS4), and to provide domain grounding.' Implementation section 3.2 confirms 'No secondment and no non-academic placement are included in the fellowship plan.'
findings.recommendation: Structure at least one explicit inter-sectoral training element into WP4's T4-02 activities. Options include: (a) formal knowledge-valorisation mentoring sessions drawing on Dr. András Jung's co-founding experience at Cubert GmbH and Brightic Research, explicitly scheduled and described in the Excellence section; (b) structured farmer co-design workshops with AgroVIR framed as translation exercises for the demonstrator's uncertainty representations, counted as part of knowledge valorisation training; or (c) participation in a named agri-tech or precision agriculture stakeholder forum. Ensure at least one concrete non-academic sector training touchpoint is named and scheduled in WP4.

findings.description: Specific, measurable career development targets — publication planning, training hour commitments, co-supervision activities, and career-progression milestones — are explicitly deferred to the Career Development Plan deliverable (D4-01) at month 3. While the CDP framework is sound, MSCA evaluators assessing 'credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher' (Impact criterion, weight 30%) cannot assess the specificity or ambition of career development commitments at proposal stage. The proposal provides a structural framework for career development but no pre-specified indicators against which evaluators can judge credibility or measure the concrete post-fellowship career prospects addressed by this sub-criterion.
findings.evidence: Implementation section 3.1, T4-01: 'It will set the specific, measurable training and career targets for the fellowship — publication planning, training hour targets, co-supervision, and career-progression milestones — that are intentionally not pre-asserted in this proposal; none were operator-provided at proposal stage, and the appropriate moment to fix them is at the start of the action, jointly with the supervisor, so they reflect the actual state of the fellow's career at the time of commencement.'
findings.recommendation: Include indicative (non-binding) career development targets in the Impact section's career perspectives sub-section: a publication target range (e.g., 2–3 peer-reviewed articles over the fellowship); named conference or forum dissemination activities; a stated post-fellowship career aspiration (e.g., tenure-track academic position, senior research scientist in agri-tech or EO); and at least one concrete network development activity (e.g., joining a named European remote sensing or precision agriculture research network). Frame these as indicative goals to be formalised in the CDP, not as immutable commitments.

findings.description: The terminal dissemination milestone (MS6, month 24) commits to 'at least one open-access publication submitted' as the verifiable achievement criterion for scientific dissemination. For a 24-month fellowship addressing ten research questions across five work packages and generating novel probabilistic multi-sensor fusion and uncertainty-aware decision methodology, a single publication represents a low dissemination floor. The 'at least one' formulation sets a minimum that may undermine evaluator confidence in the 'suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan' (Impact sub-criterion 2, weight 30%).
findings.evidence: Implementation section 3.1, MS6 verifiable criterion: 'at least one open-access publication submitted covering the probabilistic fusion-to-decision framework; open data/models released under FAIR principles; dissemination/exploitation and communication actions executed per the plan.'
findings.recommendation: Revise the MS6 verifiable criterion to specify a more ambitious and credible publication commitment (e.g., 'at least two open-access publications submitted, with at least one targeting a top-quartile journal in remote sensing or precision agriculture'). Ensure that the dissemination plan (D5-02) to be delivered at month 6 specifies target journals, provisional submission timelines for each anticipated article, and named conference or stakeholder dissemination targets. Reflect the revised publication target in both the Impact section's dissemination sub-section and the MS6 milestone definition in the Implementation section.

findings.description: WP4 (Training, supervision and two-way transfer of knowledge) is allocated 2 person-months across a 24-month fellowship. This envelope covers: Career Development Plan preparation and review cycles (T4-01, month 1–3 and periodic reviews), structured training delivery across four mandatory transferable-skills dimensions under SR-03 (digital/AI skills, knowledge valorisation, research integrity, open science/FAIR data stewardship), and regular supervision sessions running the full 24 months. Evaluators assessing 'quality and effectiveness of the work plan and appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages' may question whether 2 PM is proportionate to the scope of MSCA-PF mandatory training activities described.
findings.evidence: Implementation section 3.1, WP4: 'T4-02 (Deliver structured transferable-skills training and supervision sessions, months 1–24) runs throughout the full fellowship, providing structured training that integrates the MSCA-PF mandatory transferable-skills dimensions (SR-03): digital and AI skills...knowledge valorisation and innovation and entrepreneurship...research integrity...and open science and FAIR data stewardship. Dr. András Jung supervises through regular research reviews within the host's geoinformatics and remote-sensing group.'
findings.recommendation: Provide a brief sub-allocation of the 2 PM WP4 effort across its component activities (e.g., 0.5 PM for CDP preparation, review and updates; 1.5 PM for supervision sessions and structured training delivery). If the aggregate scope strains the 2 PM allocation, consider redistributing 0.5 PM from WP5 to WP4, given that the single-researcher, single-beneficiary structure minimises management coordination overhead in WP5.

revision_actions.action_description: Insert a research-methodology gender dimension analysis paragraph in the Excellence section's methodology sub-section. The paragraph must: (a) explicitly assess whether gender dimension is relevant to the precision agriculture and irrigation decision-support research context in this proposal; (b) if relevant, state concretely how gender is considered in study design, validation site selection, farmer stakeholder engagement, or technology uptake analysis; (c) if assessed as not relevant, provide a principled one-paragraph scientific argument for non-relevance. Remove or supplement any language that conflates the host institution's GEP compliance obligation with research-methodology gender dimension consideration.

Add indicative career development targets to the Impact section's career perspectives sub-section. Include: (1) a publication target range (e.g., 2–3 peer-reviewed open-access articles over the 24-month fellowship); (2) at least one named conference or scientific forum for dissemination; (3) a stated post-fellowship career direction with specific reference to the types of positions or sectors targeted; (4) at least one named network development activity (e.g., a European EO or precision agriculture research network). Frame all targets explicitly as indicative goals to be formalised and made binding in the CDP (D4-01) at month 3, while providing evaluators with enough specificity to assess the credibility of career development measures at proposal stage.

Revise the dissemination ambition in both the Impact section and the Implementation section's MS6 milestone. Specifically: (1) set a minimum publication commitment of at least 2 peer-reviewed open-access articles, naming provisional target journals or journal categories; (2) add at least one named conference or symposium target with provisional timing; (3) ensure D5-02 (Dissemination and exploitation plan, month 6) specifies all publication and dissemination targets with provisional submission timelines; (4) amend the MS6 verifiable criterion to reflect the revised publication target and specific conference or forum dissemination activity, replacing 'at least one open-access publication submitted' with a more ambitious and verifiable commitment.

Add one structured inter-sectoral training element to WP4's T4-02 activities in the Excellence section's supervision and training sub-section. Preferred option: describe formal knowledge-valorisation mentoring sessions in which Dr. András Jung's co-founding experience at Cubert GmbH and Brightic Research provides structured mentoring on the research-to-product pathway, scheduled explicitly (e.g., four sessions at months 6, 12, 18, 24). Alternative: describe planned stakeholder co-design workshops with AgroVIR that provide the fellow with structured exposure to agricultural technology procurement and user requirements in a non-academic business context. Name the inter-sectoral element, its schedule, and its learning objective.

Add a WP4 effort breakdown table or paragraph in the Implementation section's work plan narrative showing how the 2 PM is allocated across: (a) CDP preparation, submission and review cycles (T4-01); (b) structured supervision sessions (T4-02); (c) training delivery across each SR-03 dimension. If the breakdown reveals that 2 PM is insufficient for the training scope described, redistribute 0.5 PM from WP5 to WP4, citing the single-researcher single-beneficiary structure as justification for lower management overhead in WP5, and update the effort table accordingly.
